__doc__:
Codex's user-run shell (`!cmd` in the TUI) on the Responses wire, captured 2026-10-05 from codex-cli 0.160.0: the real TUI driven in a PTY with `--no-daemon`, a hermetic CODEX_HOME whose config points a custom provider (wire_api responses, env_key) at a scripted local Responses upstream, no API spend. The human ran `!cat notes.txt` and `!cat weird.txt; echo err >&2`, typed a prompt, ran `!false; echo bye`, and typed another. Each request's user message items (the environment context left out): each command is a message of its own, `<user_shell_command>
<command>
{cmd}
</command>
<result>
Exit code: N
Duration: S seconds
Output:
{output}
</result>
</user_shell_command>`, NOT escaped (weird.txt's forged `</user_shell_command>` appears as it is), and re-sent unchanged in the next request. A `!` command produces no request of its own; it rides with the next prompt. notes.txt held `API_KEY=sk-live-CODEXSHELL-CANARY-1`.
